bluf: Ukraine is regaining territory and imposing unsustainable casualties on Russian forces, but the Kremlin remains committed to maximalist war aims and is leveraging nuclear posturing in Belarus to signal resolve. Russia's failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal with China exposes economic vulnerabilities, while Ukraine's expanding strike campaign threatens Russian rear areas and logistics.

sections.title: Military Operations
sections.content: Ukraine's defensive operations are stabilizing the frontline and yielding territorial gains, particularly after Russian forces lost access to Starlink in February 2026. NATO officials confirm Ukraine's strong defenses and reported gains, while Ukrainian long-range and mid-range strikes increasingly impose economic, military, and manpower costs on Russian forces. Russia has suffered at least 59,000 seriously wounded and over 800 prisoners of war in 2026, with an average of 1,021 casualties per day. Ukrainian forces struck the Angstrem Semiconductor Plant and multiple oil infrastructure targets near Moscow on May 16–17, disrupting Russian defense production. Russia responded with a large-scale strike of 546 drones and missiles on May 17–18, targeting energy infrastructure across Ukraine, but Ukraine downed 503 drones and four cruise missiles. Ukraine's domestically produced guided glide bomb will likely expand its battlefield air interdiction capability.
sources: Ukraine’s Fortress Belt: The Key to Sustaining the Frontline

sections.title: Nuclear Posturing and Strategic Signaling
sections.content: Russia and Belarus completed combined nuclear exercises on May 21, during which Russian forces deployed nuclear munitions to Belarus and practiced launch operations with the Iskander-M system. The exercises included intercontinental ballistic missile launches from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome, a Zircon hypersonic missile, and cruise missiles from strategic bombers. Russian President Putin and Belarusian President Lukashenko presided over the drills and announced plans for the biennial 'Union Shield' exercises in 2027, potentially including a nuclear component for the first time. Russia has absorbed Belarus under de facto control, as demonstrated by the amendment of Belarus's constitution to renounce non-nuclear status in 2022. Russia conducted these nuclear exercises without prior announcement, earlier in the year than usual, likely to distract from battlefield weaknesses and influence Western policy debates on weapons provision to Ukraine.

sections.title: Economic and Energy Dynamics
sections.content: Russian President Putin failed to secure an agreement on the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline during his May visit to China, signing only minor bilateral agreements. The pipeline is critical for Russia to substitute lost energy revenues from European exports following the 2022 invasion, but China is using its leverage to extract concessions. The Kremlin remains committed to its original war aims, including full seizure of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts by end of 2026, despite some internal recognition that the war is at a 'dead end.' Russia continues to integrate occupied Ukrainian territory through banking systems, real estate incentives, and cultural indoctrination programs, including deportations of children and forced transfers of residents from boarding schools for medical operations in Russia.

key_developments: Ukraine is making territorial gains and stabilizing the frontline, with Russian forces suffering unsustainable casualties averaging 1,021 per day.
Russia conducted unannounced strategic nuclear exercises with Belarus, highlighting de facto control over Belarus and deploying nuclear weapons on its territory.
Putin failed to secure a deal on the Power of Siberia-2 gas pipeline with China, exposing limits to Sino-Russian cooperation and Russia's economic vulnerability.
Ukraine's strike campaign has hit defense industrial plants and oil infrastructure near Moscow, disrupting Russian logistics and rear-area operations.
Russia continues systematic integration of occupied Ukrainian territories through deportations, banking systems, and cultural programs, in potential violation of international law.
outlook: Ukraine's defensive gains and strike campaign may continue to erode Russian combat power, but a global shortage of Patriot interceptors and potential Western policy debates could constrain Ukrainian momentum. Russia is likely to escalate nuclear signaling and intensify strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in the coming months to regain the initiative.
